artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed, oriented $3$-manifold. A plane field $\xi$ on $M$ is a cooriented $2$-plane subbundle of $TM$; equivalently it is the kernel of a nonvanishing $1$-form $\alpha$. Such a $\xi$ is a contact structure if $\alpha\wedge d\alpha$ is nowhere zero, and the sign of the contact structure is the sign of $\alpha\wedge d\alpha$ relative to the orientation of $M$. A contact structure $\xi$ is tight if there is no embedded disk $D\hookrightarrow M$ such that $TD|_{\partial D}=\xi|_{\partial D}$ but $TD\ne\xi$ along $\partial D$ (i.e., it contains no overtwisted disk). Two contact structures are homotopic as plane fields if they are homotopic through cooriented $2$-plane fields on $M$.

A cooriented $C^0$-foliation on $M$ is a cooriented $2$-dimensional foliation whose tangent plane field is continuous; it is Reebless if it contains no Reeb component (no embedded solid torus whose boundary is a leaf and whose interior is foliated by planes spiraling onto the boundary).

Suppose $(\xi_-,\xi_+)$ is a pair of cooriented contact structures on $M$ with opposite signs that are homotopic as plane fields, and suppose both $\xi_-$ and $\xi_+$ are tight. Must $M$ admit a cooriented Reebless $C^0$-foliation?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a recent problem list on foliations and diffeomorphism groups (2026) and is posed as an open question. No published resolution was located in the search; results of Eliashberg–Thurston, Bowden, and Kazez–Roberts give related approximation theorems but do not resolve this converse-type question.

status_evidence.title: Problem List on Foliations and Diffeomorphism groups
status_evidence.snippet: Question 2.8 asks whether the existence of two tight contact structures with opposite signs that are homotopic as plane fields implies the existence of a cooriented Reebless C^0-foliation.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open question in a 2026 problem list.

status_evidence.title: Contact perturbations of Reebless foliations are universally tight
status_evidence.snippet: Bowden's theorem: Reebless C^0-foliations are approximated by universally tight contact structures of both signs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides one direction of the relationship motivating the question.
